patch_description: The crossover combines the two variants: the greedy heap-based `balanced_packing` from the first program (which produces optimal-ish balanced packing and showed the best algorithm/inference time profile, times_inference 0.98) with the vectorized `replicate_experts` and the shared hierarchical `rebalance_experts_hierarchical` / `rebalance_experts` scaffolding that both programs use identically. The heap-based greedy packing assigns each item (in descending weight order) to the lightest non-full pack, giving better balance guarantees than the purely vectorized snake packing when pack counts vary, while moving list conversion outside the loop (converting weight/indices to Python lists once, then building tensors once at the end) keeps it fast. This keeps identical inputs/outputs while improving both balance quality and runtime versus the snake variant's slow algorithm time.
